case_studies.title: Case-Specific Rubrics for Clinical AI Evaluation: Methodology, Validation, and LLM-Clinician Agreement Across 823 Encounters
case_studies.abstract: Objective. Clinical AI documentation systems require evaluation methodologies that are clinically valid, economically viable, and sensitive to iterative changes. Methods requiring expert review per scoring instance are too slow and expensive for safe, iterative deployment. We present a case-specific, clinician-authored rubric methodology for clinical AI evaluation and examine whether LLM-generated rubrics can approximate clinician agreement. Materials and Methods. Twenty clinicians authored 1,646 rubrics for 823 clinical cases (736 real-world, 87 synthetic) across primary care, psychiatry, onc
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating clinical AI documentation systems is addressed through the development of case-specific rubrics. The AI approach involves using large language models (LLMs) to generate rubrics that approximate clinician agreement. The outcome shows that LLM-generated rubrics can be a viable alternative to expert review for clinical AI evaluation.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can use LLMs to generate case-specific rubrics for clinical AI evaluation, reducing the need for expert review and increasing the efficiency of the evaluation process. By using this methodology, practitioners can validate the performance of clinical AI systems and identify areas for improvement.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of case-specific rubrics for clinical AI evaluation can be monetized through the creation of a software platform that provides automated evaluation and feedback for clinical AI systems. This platform can be sold to healthcare organizations, offering a cost-effective and efficient solution for evaluating and improving the performance of clinical AI systems.

case_studies.title: Leveraging LLMs for Multi-File DSL Code Generation: An Industrial Case Study
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform strongly on general-purpose code generation, yet their applicability to enterprise domain-specific languages (DSLs) remains underexplored, especially for repository-scale change generation spanning multiple files and folder structures from a single natural-language (NL) instruction. We report an industrial case study at BMW that adapts code-oriented LLMs to generate and modify project-root DSL artifacts for an Xtext-based DSL that drives downstream Java/TypeScript code generation. We develop an end-to-end pipeline for dataset construction, multi-file task r
case_studies.summary: The problem of generating and modifying domain-specific languages (DSLs) for enterprise applications is addressed through the use of large language models (LLMs). The AI approach involves adapting code-oriented LLMs to generate and modify project-root DSL artifacts for an Xtext-based DSL. The outcome of this industrial case study at BMW demonstrates the potential of LLMs for multi-file DSL code generation, paving the way for increased efficiency and productivity in software development.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can develop end-to-end pipelines for dataset construction and multi-file task generation, and adapt code-oriented LLMs to their specific use cases. By leveraging LLMs, practitioners can automate repetitive coding tasks and improve the overall quality of their software development processes.
case_studies.monetisation: The monetisation potential of this approach lies in its ability to increase efficiency and productivity in software development, which can lead to cost savings and improved time-to-market for enterprises. A concrete business opportunity could be to develop a product or service that provides LLM-based DSL code generation capabilities to enterprises, either as a standalone tool or as part of a larger software development platform.

case_studies.title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are promising for generalist robot control, but on-robot deployment is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. Most prior evaluations rely on desktop-grade GPUs, obscuring the trade-offs and opportunities offered by heterogeneous edge accelerators (GPUs/XPUs/NPUs). We present a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization. First, we build a cross-accelerator leaderboard and evaluate model-hardware pairs under CET (Cost, Energy, Time), showing that right-sized edge devices can be more
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying Vision-Language-Action models on robots is hindered by real-time inference constraints and tight cost and energy budgets. To address this, the authors propose a model-hardware co-characterization approach, evaluating model-hardware pairs under Cost, Energy, and Time metrics. The outcome shows that right-sized edge devices can be more efficient than desktop-grade GPUs, enabling potential on-robot deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can build a cross-accelerator leaderboard to evaluate model-hardware pairs and identify the most efficient combinations for their specific use case. By considering the Cost, Energy, and Time metrics, practitioners can optimize their models for on-robot deployment and achieve real-time inference under tight budgets.
case_studies.monetisation: The research offers a concrete business opportunity for companies developing robot control systems, as the proposed approach can enable more efficient and cost-effective deployment of Vision-Language-Action models. By leveraging the findings of this study, companies can create more competitive products with improved performance and reduced energy consumption, targeting applications such as service robotics, autonomous vehicles, or industrial automation.
case_studies.relevance_tag: AI Agents, Automation, Computer Vision, NLP, MLOps

case_studies.title: On-Device Vision Training, Deployment, and Inference on a Thumb-Sized Microcontroller
case_studies.abstract: This paper presents a complete, end-to-end on-device vision machine learning pipeline, comprising data acquisition, two-layer CNN training with Adam optimization, and real-time inference, executing entirely on a microcontroller-class device costing $15-40 USD. Unlike cloud-based workflows that require external infrastructure and conceal the computational pipeline from the practitioner, this system implements every step of the core ML lifecycle in approximately 1,750 lines of readable C++ that compiles in under one minute using the Arduino IDE, with no external ML dependencies. Running on the S
case_studies.summary: The problem of relying on cloud-based workflows for machine learning is addressed by developing an on-device vision machine learning pipeline. The AI approach involves using a two-layer CNN with Adam optimization, trained and deployed on a microcontroller-class device. The outcome is a complete, end-to-end pipeline executing entirely on a low-cost device, demonstrating the potential for real-time inference and local processing.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this lesson by exploring the use of microcontroller-class devices for on-device machine learning, allowing for more efficient and private data processing. By leveraging accessible tools like the Arduino IDE, developers can create and deploy machine learning models without relying on cloud infrastructure or external dependencies.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of this on-device vision pipeline presents a concrete business opportunity for companies looking to create low-cost, edge-based computer vision products. Potential applications include smart home devices, industrial automation, and wearable technology, where real-time processing and local decision-making are critical.

case_studies.title: A Deployable Embodied Vision-Language Navigation System with Hierarchical Cognition and Context-Aware Exploration
case_studies.abstract: Bridging the gap between embodied intelligence and embedded deployment remains a key challenge in intelligent robotic systems, where perception, reasoning, and planning must operate under strict constraints on computation, memory, energy, and real-time execution. In vision-language navigation (VLN), existing approaches often face a fundamental trade-off between strong reasoning capabilities and efficient deployment on real-world platforms. In this paper, we present a deployable embodied VLN system that achieves both high efficiency and robust high-level reasoning on real-world robotic platform
case_studies.summary: The problem of bridging the gap between embodied intelligence and embedded deployment in intelligent robotic systems is addressed by proposing a deployable embodied vision-language navigation system. The AI approach involves hierarchical cognition and context-aware exploration to achieve both high efficiency and robust high-level reasoning. The outcome is a system that can operate on real-world robotic platforms with strict constraints on computation, memory, energy, and real-time execution.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on designing hierarchical cognitive architectures that integrate perception, reasoning, and planning capabilities. Additionally, they can explore context-aware exploration strategies to improve the efficiency and robustness of their embodied AI systems.
case_studies.monetisation: A concrete business opportunity for this technology is in the development of autonomous robots for industries such as logistics, healthcare, and manufacturing, where efficient and robust navigation systems are crucial. Companies can leverage this technology to create products such as autonomous warehouse robots or self-navigating robots for healthcare facilities.

case_studies.title: Cortex 2.0: Grounding World Models in Real-World Industrial Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Industrial robotic manipulation demands reliable long-horizon execution across embodiments, tasks, and changing object distributions. While Vision-Language-Action models have demonstrated strong generalization, they remain fundamentally reactive. By optimizing the next action given the current observation without evaluating potential futures, they are brittle to the compounding failure modes of long-horizon tasks. Cortex 2.0 shifts from reactive control to plan-and-act by generating candidate future trajectories in visual latent space, scoring them for expected success and efficiency, then com
case_studies.summary: Industrial robotic manipulation tasks require reliable long-horizon execution, but current Vision-Language-Action models are reactive and brittle to failure modes. Cortex 2.0 addresses this by generating candidate future trajectories in visual latent space, scoring them for expected success and efficiency, and then executing the best plan. This approach enables more robust and efficient task execution in industrial settings.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on developing models that can generate and evaluate potential future trajectories, rather than just reacting to the current observation. By incorporating planning and evaluation into the decision-making process, AI systems can become more reliable and efficient in complex, real-world environments.
case_studies.monetisation: The Cortex 2.0 approach has significant monetisation potential in the industrial automation sector, where reliable and efficient robotic manipulation is crucial for manufacturing and logistics operations. Companies can leverage this technology to develop more advanced and autonomous robotic systems, leading to increased productivity and reduced costs in various industries.

case_studies.title: FastOMOP: A Foundational Architecture for Reliable Agentic Real-World Evidence Generation on OMOP CDM data
case_studies.abstract: The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM), maintained by the Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics (OHDSI) collaboration, enabled the harmonisation of electronic health records data of nearly one billion patients in 83 countries. Yet generating real-world evidence (RWE) from these repositories remains a manual process requiring clinical, epidemiological and technical expertise. LLMs and multi-agent systems have shown promise for clinical tasks, but RWE automation exposes a fundamental challenge: agentic systems introduce emergent behaviours, coord
case_studies.summary: The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM) has enabled the harmonisation of electronic health records data, but generating real-world evidence (RWE) from these repositories remains a manual process. The proposed FastOMOP architecture aims to address this challenge by leveraging AI and multi-agent systems to automate RWE generation. The outcome of this approach could potentially streamline the process of generating RWE, reducing the need for manual expertise and increasing the efficiency of clinical and epidemiological research.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can explore the use of multi-agent systems and LLMs to automate tasks in other domains, such as healthcare or finance, where data harmonisation and evidence generation are critical. By leveraging the FastOMOP architecture as a foundational model, practitioners can develop more efficient and reliable systems for generating real-world evidence.
case_studies.monetisation: The FastOMOP architecture presents a concrete business opportunity for companies operating in the healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors, where the automation of RWE generation can significantly reduce costs and improve the speed of clinical trials. By developing a product or service based on the FastOMOP architecture, companies can offer a competitive advantage in the market, enabling them to generate high-quality RWE more efficiently and effectively.

case_studies.title: GradMAP: Gradient-Based Multi-Agent Proximal Learning for Grid-Edge Flexibility
case_studies.abstract: Coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices requires learning methods that remain fully decentralised in deployment while still respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics. This paper proposes gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning (GradMAP) to address this challenge. GradMAP trains independent neural-network policies for each agent without any parameter sharing, and each agent uses only its own local observation for online decision-making without communication. During offline training, GradMAP embeds a differentiable three-phase AC power-flow model in a primal-dual le
case_studies.summary: The problem of coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices in a decentralized manner while respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics is addressed. The AI approach proposes GradMAP, a gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning method that trains independent neural-network policies for each agent. The outcome is a fully decentralized learning method that enables online decision-making without communication among agents.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the GradMAP method to other decentralized control problems by embedding differentiable physical models in a primal-dual learning framework. This approach can be used to develop scalable and adaptive control systems for various applications, including smart grids and IoT devices.
case_studies.monetisation: The GradMAP method has the potential to be monetized as a software solution for grid management companies, enabling them to optimize their grid operations and improve efficiency. A company can be founded to develop and deploy this solution, providing a competitive advantage in the smart grid market.

case_studies.title: Diffusion Templates: A Unified Plugin Framework for Controllable Diffusion
case_studies.abstract: Controllable diffusion methods have substantially expanded the practical utility of diffusion models, but they are typically developed as isolated, backbone-specific systems with incompatible training pipelines, parameter formats, and runtime hooks. This fragmentation makes it difficult to reuse infrastructure across tasks, transfer capabilities across backbones, or compose multiple controls within a single generation pipeline. We present Diffusion Templates, a unified and open plugin framework that decouples base-model inference from controllable capability injection. The framework is organiz
case_studies.summary: The problem of fragmented controllable diffusion methods is addressed by introducing a unified plugin framework. The AI approach involves decoupling base-model inference from controllable capability injection, allowing for a more modular and adaptable system. The outcome is a framework that enables the reuse of infrastructure, transfer of capabilities, and composition of multiple controls within a single generation pipeline.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this framework by identifying areas where controllable diffusion methods can be unified and modularized, allowing for greater flexibility and adaptability in their models. By using a plugin-based approach, practitioners can reduce the complexity and fragmentation of their systems, making it easier to develop and deploy controllable diffusion methods.
case_studies.monetisation: The Diffusion Templates framework presents a clear product opportunity for companies looking to develop and deploy controllable diffusion methods, particularly in industries where adaptability and flexibility are crucial. By commercializing this framework, companies can provide a unified platform for developers to build and integrate controllable diffusion models, generating revenue through licensing, support, and services.

case_studies.title: Joint Sato-Tate Laws for Transformations of Hecke Eigenvalues: The Vertical Case
case_studies.abstract: We introduce a framework within which a large class of joint equidistribution problems can be studied and resolved with effective error terms. This involves proving a higher dimensional and $μ$-analogue of the Erdös-Turán inequality, and utilizing the theory of the Hardy-Krause (H-K) variation from analysis, where, in particular, we formulate a technique to approximate a broad class of relevant functions by functions of bounded H-K variation. Our main focus will be on the vertical Sato-Tate problem for spaces of cusp forms and for families of elliptic curves over finite fields. In particular,
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the joint equidistribution of Hecke eigenvalues in the context of number theory, specifically the vertical Sato-Tate problem. The AI approach involves developing a framework that utilizes the theory of Hardy-Krause variation and formulates a technique to approximate relevant functions. The outcome is a proof of a higher dimensional and μ-analogue of the Erdös-Turán inequality, providing effective error terms for a large class of joint equidistribution problems.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by utilizing the developed framework to tackle similar problems in number theory and analysis, leveraging the power of mathematical techniques to drive innovation. By understanding the application of Hardy-Krause variation and function approximation, practitioners can develop more effective solutions to complex problems.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this research is the development of advanced mathematical software or consulting services that leverage the findings to solve real-world problems in fields such as cryptography or coding theory. Companies specializing in mathematical modeling or computational number theory could adapt the techniques and results from this study to create innovative products or services.

case_studies.title: Learning to Think from Multiple Thinkers
case_studies.abstract: We study learning with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers, all of whom provide correct but possibly systematically different solutions, e.g., step-by-step solutions to math problems written by different thinkers, or step-by-step execution traces of different programs solving the same problem. We consider classes that are computationally easy to learn using CoT supervision from a single thinker, but hard to learn with only end-result supervision, i.e., without CoT (Joshi et al. 2025). We establish that, under cryptographic assumptions, learning can be hard from CoT superv
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the difficulty of learning from Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers, which can provide systematically different solutions to the same problem. The AI approach involves analyzing the learning process with CoT supervision from multiple thinkers and establishing the hardness of learning under cryptographic assumptions. The outcome of this study is a deeper understanding of the limitations of learning with CoT supervision from multiple thinkers.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by considering the potential limitations of learning from multiple sources, especially when the sources provide systematically different solutions. To overcome these limitations, practitioners can explore techniques such as data augmentation, regularization, or ensemble methods to improve the robustness of their models.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity based on this study is the development of AI-powered educational tools that can learn from multiple sources and provide personalized step-by-step solutions to students. Such tools could be monetized through subscription-based models or licensing agreements with educational institutions.

case_studies.title: Benchmarking Source-Sensitive Reasoning in Turkish: Humans and LLMs under Evidential Trust Manipulation
case_studies.abstract: This paper investigates whether source trustworthiness shapes Turkish evidential morphology and whether large language models (LLMs) track this sensitivity. We study the past-domain contrast between -DI and -mIs in controlled cloze contexts where the information source is overtly external, while only its perceived reliability is manipulated (High-Trust vs. Low-Trust). In a human production experiment, native speakers of Turkish show a robust trust effect: High-Trust contexts yield relatively more -DI, whereas Low-Trust contexts yield relatively more -mIs, with the pattern remaining stable acro
case_studies.summary: The study investigates how source trustworthiness affects Turkish evidential morphology and whether large language models (LLMs) can track this sensitivity. The researchers used a human production experiment and controlled cloze contexts to manipulate the perceived reliability of the information source. The results show a robust trust effect, with High-Trust contexts yielding more -DI and Low-Trust contexts yielding more -mIs, indicating that LLMs can be sensitive to source trustworthiness.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this research, AI practitioners can use the findings to improve the performance of LLMs in tasks that require understanding the trustworthiness of information sources. By incorporating source sensitivity into LLMs, practitioners can develop more accurate and reliable language models that can better handle complex linguistic contexts.
case_studies.monetisation: The research has potential monetisation opportunities in the development of more accurate language translation tools and chatbots that can understand the nuances of human language and adapt to different contexts. Companies can use these findings to create more sophisticated language processing systems that can improve customer engagement and provide more effective language-based services.

case_studies.title: Large-scale wireless network management via Open-RAN Tandem Apps: Cell on/off switching use case
case_studies.abstract: With growing mobile-network complexity, management and optimization have become increasingly difficult. Centralized algorithms face high control-data overhead and computational load, while distributed approaches often perform far from optimally. The O-RAN architecture introduces two tiers of RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs), enabling hierarchical network-management schemes. This work proposes Tandem Apps: a pair of tightly coupled optimization mechanisms running on both controllers. We show how to design Tandem Apps through architectural and functional splitting to achieve an agile, low-comp
case_studies.summary: The increasing complexity of mobile networks makes management and optimization challenging, with centralized algorithms facing high control-data overhead and distributed approaches performing suboptimally. This work proposes Tandem Apps, a pair of tightly coupled optimization mechanisms running on both RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs) in the O-RAN architecture. The outcome is an agile, low-complexity network management scheme, but the study lacks concrete metrics and implementation details.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners should explores the potential of hierarchical network management schemes using O-RAN architecture and RICs. They should also investigate the design of Tandem Apps through architectural and functional splitting to achieve agile and low-complexity optimization mechanisms.
case_studies.monetisation: The concept of Tandem Apps has potential for monetization in the telecom industry, particularly in the development of optimized network management solutions for mobile networks. However, the lack of clear metrics and implementation details makes it challenging to estimate the concrete business opportunity at this stage.

case_studies.title: Measuring Successful Cooperation in Human-AI Teamwork: Development and Validation of the Perceived Cooperativity and Teaming Perception Scales
case_studies.abstract: As human-AI cooperation becomes increasingly prevalent, reliable instruments for assessing the subjective quality of cooperative human-AI interaction are needed. We introduce two theoretically grounded scales: the Perceived Cooperativity Scale (PCS), grounded in joint activity theory, and the Teaming Perception Scale (TPS), grounded in evolutionary cooperation theory. The PCS captures an agent's perceived cooperative capability and practice within a single interaction sequence; the TPS captures the emergent sense of teaming arising from mutual contribution and support. Both scales were adapted
case_studies.summary: The problem of measuring successful cooperation in human-AI teamwork is addressed through the development of two scales: the Perceived Cooperativity Scale and the Teaming Perception Scale. The AI approach uses joint activity theory and evolutionary cooperation theory to ground these scales. The outcome is the introduction of two theoretically grounded scales for assessing the subjective quality of cooperative human-AI interaction.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this research, AI practitioners can use the Perceived Cooperativity Scale and the Teaming Perception Scale to evaluate the effectiveness of their human-AI teamwork systems. By incorporating these scales into their system design and evaluation, practitioners can improve the cooperative capabilities of their AI systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The research has potential for monetisation in the development of more effective human-AI teamwork systems, which can be applied in various industries such as healthcare, finance, and education. Companies can use the Perceived Cooperativity Scale and the Teaming Perception Scale to assess and improve the performance of their human-AI teams, leading to increased productivity and efficiency.

case_studies.title: Multiple positive solutions with prescribed masses for a coupled Schrödinger system: mass mixed and Sobolev critical coupled case
case_studies.abstract: The aim of this paper is to establish multiple positive normalized solutions $(u,v,λ_1,λ_2)\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N,\mathbb{R}^2)\times \mathbb{R}^2$ to the following coupled Schrödinger system involving Sobolev critical exponent: $$ \begin{cases} -Δu+λ_1 u=μ_1|u|^{p-2}u+να|u|^{α-2}u|v|^β, x\in \mathbb{R}^N,\\ -Δv+λ_2 v=μ_2|v|^{q-2}v+νβ|v|^{β-2}v|u|^α, x\in \mathbb{R}^N,\\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|u|^2\mathrm{d}x=a, \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|v|^2\mathrm{d}x=b, \end{cases} N\geq 3, $$ where $μ_1,μ_2, ν, a, b>0$. We are particularly interested in the mass mixed case that $2<p, q<2+\frac{4}{N}, α>1, β>1$, and $
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this paper is the existence of multiple positive normalized solutions to a coupled Schrödinger system with prescribed masses. The AI approach used is a theoretical analysis of the system using mathematical techniques such as the Nehari manifold and the fountain theorem. The outcome is the establishment of the existence of multiple positive solutions under certain conditions.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this paper by using similar mathematical techniques to analyze complex systems and establish the existence of solutions. The use of the Nehari manifold and the fountain theorem can be particularly useful in analyzing systems with multiple variables and nonlinear interactions.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this research is the development of new materials or systems that exploit the properties of coupled Schrödinger systems. Companies specializing in materials science or quantum technology could potentially benefit from the insights gained from this research, leading to the development of new products or applications.
